weeks.rationale: Re-anchor week, 14 weeks to Hyrox #2 and the opening week of the aggressive volume ramp (base_weekly_km raised 53 -> 62, band now 55.8-68.2 km). Tuesday's threshold session is replaced by a 30-minute field time trial: the zones every prescription depends on were measured on 2026-06-19 and the whole macrocycle is about to be calibrated to them, so testing at this block boundary while still fresh off the race taper is worth more than one more threshold workout. Volume steps to 62.5 km, mid-band rather than top, because the test needs fresh legs and this is already a large jump from the post-race week. Everything after Tuesday should be re-targeted to whatever the TT returns.
weeks.methodology: Testing before prescribing: a lab-anchored pace is only as good as its age, and a threshold that has improved silently makes every subsequent session too easy, which is the failure mode a flat-band plan hides best. The 30-minute TT is the standard field proxy for LT2 - average pace across the effort approximates threshold pace and average HR over the final twenty minutes approximates LTHR - and it doubles as a genuine threshold stimulus, so nothing is lost from the week's training even if the numbers come back unchanged. Around it the week stays polarized, with one hard day, one moderate station day, and the rest genuinely easy. The new gym-daily and home-treadmill availability is used to place gym work in the morning and running in the afternoon rather than to lengthen single runs, which is what keeps a 22% volume jump absorbable.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic (PM)
sessions.prescription: PM (home treadmill or outdoors): 56 min genuinely easy, HR <=138 bpm, conversational. NO gym today - leave the legs alone before Tuesday's time trial.
sessions.purpose: Aerobic volume with zero residual fatigue carried into the time trial.
sessions.why: Easy km is the cheapest volume in the week and carries a big share of the new 62.5 km target, so it is lengthened rather than the quality days. The gym visit is deliberately skipped despite being available every day: a test is only useful if it is run fresh, and lifting the day before would confound the single measurement that recalibrates the next thirteen weeks.

sessions.title: 30-min Threshold TT (BENCHMARK) + Heavy Lower (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no gym) BENCHMARK - 30-MIN TIME TRIAL: 20 min easy warmup with 3x1 min builds (~3.5 km) -> 30 min all-out time trial, even effort, run as a race (~6.8 km). Press lap at 10 min: average HR over the FINAL 20 MIN = your LTHR, average pace over the full 30 min = your threshold pace. TREADMILL at 1% incline, no handrails, FAN ON YOU (indoor heat stress inflates HR and HR is half the measurement). Self-paced steps: start 13.5 km/h; at 10 min +0.5 if RPE<=7; at 20 min +0.5 if still holding form; empty it over the last 5. Read TOTAL DISTANCE off the console at 30:00 -> threshold pace = 30 / distance. Note which treadmill - every future re-test must use the same one. -> 15 min easy cooldown (~2.6 km). PM (gym, maintenance only): back squat 3x3 @ 100 kg, trap-bar deadlift 2x3 @ 130 kg. No plyometrics, no hip thrust. LOG THE TT RESULT - the block's remaining zones depend on it.

steps.target: all-out but EVEN - start 13.5 km/h, step +0.5 at 10 and 20 min
avg HR of final 20 min = LTHR; avg pace of full 30 min = threshold pace

sessions.purpose: Re-anchor LTHR and threshold pace with a field test, while delivering a full threshold stimulus.
sessions.why: The zones driving every run in this plan are seven weeks old and were never re-checked after the race block; if LT2 has moved, every threshold session for the next thirteen weeks is prescribed too slow and the highest-ROI lever quietly stops working. A 30-min TT costs nothing in training terms because a maximal 30-minute effort IS a threshold session, so this is a free measurement rather than a week spent testing. Lifting is cut to two top-end movements rather than the usual three: the day already contains a maximal effort, and the point of the PM session is to hold strength, not add to it.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 50 min genuinely easy, HR <=138 bpm (or below the NEW easy cap if the TT moved your zones). Pure recovery after a maximal effort.
sessions.purpose: Recovery running that separates the time trial from Thursday's station work.
sessions.why: Kept strictly easy and deliberately not extended, because Tuesday was a maximal effort and Thursday still has to be run with quality. If the TT shifted your HR zones, re-anchor this run's cap to the new numbers rather than the old 138 bpm - that recalibration is the entire reason the test was run.

sessions.title: Base Compromised Sim (4 rounds)
sessions.prescription: AM (gym): 10 min easy warmup with drills (~1.7 km) -> 4 rounds of 1000 m compromised run @ ~5:05/km (147-157 bpm) into one station: R1 ski erg 1000 m; R2 sled push 202 kg / 50 m; R3 farmers carry 2x32 kg / 200 m; R4 wall balls 9 kg x 50 to 3.0 m. Walk only as far as the next station. 5 min jog cooldown (~0.8 km).
sessions.purpose: Rehearse running mechanics under station fatigue at competition loads and controlled effort.
sessions.why: Transition skill - how little pace is lost leaving a station - is what Hyrox is decided on, and it decays without weekly practice, so it stays in even during base. Effort is capped at moderate rather than raced because the week already spent its hard day on the time trial, and a second maximal day would compromise the volume ramp this block is built around. No PM run added despite the treadmill being free: extra km belongs on the easy days, not stacked onto the second-hardest session.

sessions.title: Easy + Plyo Primer (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (gym, ~15 min): box jumps 4x3 + hurdle hops 3x5, full recovery between sets, explosive snap only - stop the moment ground contact slows. PM (home treadmill or outdoors): 45 min easy, HR <=138 bpm.
sessions.purpose: Plyometric dose for tendon stiffness and running economy, plus easy aerobic km.
sessions.why: Plyometrics improve economy through elastic recoil rather than aerobic adaptation, which makes them cheap to keep but only worth doing on fresh legs - hence an easy day, never Tuesday. Jumps go in the morning and the run in the afternoon so the explosive work happens first, when the nervous system is freshest; running beforehand would blunt exactly the quality being trained. Volume held to 27 contacts so Saturday's long run starts clean.

sessions.title: Long Run
sessions.prescription: 92 min continuous, aerobic throughout. First 30 min <=138 bpm, then settle into 138-145 bpm (~5:30-5:50/km) for 50 min, last 12 min easy back down. No race-pace work this week.
sessions.purpose: The week's largest single aerobic stimulus and the base for both the 21k and Hyrox running halves.
sessions.why: Long-run duration raises LT2 from below through peripheral adaptation while threshold work raises it from above, so this and Tuesday are complementary rather than duplicative. Held purely aerobic with no race-pace finish because the week already contains a maximal time trial, and a third quality touch in the opening week of a 22% volume jump is how a ramp turns into an injury. The finish returns at the end of the block.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Optional light mobility or an easy walk. Log the TT numbers if you have not already.
sessions.purpose: Full recovery to absorb the first week of the raised volume band.
sessions.why: Adaptation happens on the rest day, and a genuine full stop is what makes six training days at this new volume sustainable rather than merely survivable. Kept completely empty despite the gym being available, because the week already carries five runs and a maximal test.

weeks.rationale: Third base week of the Nov 14 macrocycle re-entry, 13 weeks out. Volume sits at the top of the band (~58 km) with the standard base shape: one threshold session, one compromised sim, a long run, and easy volume carrying the rest. Nothing is peaked here — the job is accumulating easy kilometres and holding one quality touch per system.
weeks.methodology: Base weeks are built on a large easy fraction with a small, potent dose of hard work, which is the robust finding across elite endurance training. One threshold session anchored on the measured LT2 raises the ceiling both the 21k and the race's running share. Heavy compound strength supports running economy and is paired with the hard run so the easy days stay clean, while plyometrics sit on an easy-run day because same-session concurrent training is the one place power is meaningfully blunted. Volume steps up gradually rather than spiking.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 50 min easy, HR <=138 bpm, no faster than 5:22/km. Conversational throughout.
sessions.purpose: Open the week with unambiguous easy volume.
sessions.why: Easy kilometres are the bulk of what raises aerobic base; keeping them strictly below the Z2 ceiling is what makes tomorrow's threshold session sharp. No pickups — the grey zone buys nothing.

sessions.title: Threshold 5x6' + Heavy Lower (double)
sessions.prescription: RUN: 15 min easy warmup -> 5x6 min at threshold (155-163 bpm, 4:48-4:34/km) with 2 min jog recovery -> 10 min cooldown. GYM (separate session, same day): back squat 4x3 @ 100 kg RPE 8; trap-bar deadlift 3x3 @ 130 kg RPE 8; hip thrust 3x8 @ 110 kg. Full 2-3 min rest, explosive concentric, never to failure. Add load on any lift where the top set leaves more than 2 reps in reserve.

steps.target: RPE 7-8, 2 min rest, squeeze at lockout

sessions.purpose: Raise LT2 and load the posterior chain on one consolidated hard day.
sessions.why: Threshold is the highest-return lever for both goals, and 30 min of work is a full base-week dose without tipping into a session that needs two days to clear. The lift shares the day so the easy days stay genuinely easy; no plyometrics here because explosive work loses most in the same session as a hard run.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 45 min easy, HR <=138 bpm. Pure recovery from Tuesday's double.
sessions.purpose: Recover between the week's two quality days.
sessions.why: The day after a hard double has to be genuinely easy or the sim on Thursday degrades; this is where the polarized distribution is won or lost.

sessions.title: Base Compromised Sim (4 rounds)
sessions.prescription: 10 min warmup -> 4 rounds of 1000 m at ~4:50-4:55/km straight into one station: R1 sled push 202 kg / 50 m; R2 sled pull 153 kg / 50 m; R3 farmers carry 2x32 kg / 200 m; R4 wall balls 9 kg x 40 to 3.0 m. 5 min jog cooldown.
sessions.purpose: Train running economy under station-induced fatigue at competition loads.
sessions.why: Compromised running is the race-specific demand no pure run reproduces, and station loads stay at the Pro standard so the neuromuscular cost matches race day. Four rounds is a base-week dose — enough to keep the pattern, short of the five-round sims that belong in a peak week.

sessions.title: Easy + Plyo + Heavy Upper (double)
sessions.prescription: RUN: 45 min easy, HR <=138 bpm. GYM (separate session, same day): box jump 4x3 and standing broad jump 3x3, full recovery between sets, maximum intent. Then weighted pull-up 4x4 and overhead press 4x4 at RPE 8. Upper loads are still unbaselined — pick the weight that leaves 1-2 reps in reserve, log what you actually used, and report it so the numbers get fixed in config.

steps.target: full recovery, maximum intent, land soft
RPE 8 (~2 RIR) — log the load used

sessions.purpose: Explosive and upper-body strength on an easy-run day, plus easy volume.
sessions.why: Plyometrics improve running economy but lose most of their effect when stacked on a hard run, so they belong here on an easy day. Vertical pull and press carry directly to the pulling and overhead stations. Loads are RPE-anchored rather than prescribed in kg because the upper-body baseline has not been reported yet.

sessions.title: Long Run
sessions.prescription: 16 km steady, HR <=145 bpm for the first 13 km, then the last 3 km lifted to tempo (147-155 bpm, ~5:04-4:48/km). Check Pa:HR decoupling afterwards — target is under 5%.
sessions.purpose: Build aerobic durability and practise running strong on tired legs.
sessions.why: The long run is the single biggest contributor to the easy-volume base, and the tempo finish trains holding pace as fatigue accumulates without turning the day into a third hard session. Decoupling under 5% is the read on whether the base is actually deepening.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Mobility and sleep.
sessions.purpose: Absorb the week.
sessions.why: Adaptation happens on the rest day; a single full day off is what makes a 58 km week with two quality sessions repeatable rather than a spike.

weeks.rationale: Absorb week, 12 weeks to Hyrox #2. Volume eases to 60.5 km after three weeks at the raised band, while threshold work steps up a rung to 4x8'. The station session shortens to three rounds and rotates onto the pulling and lunging movements the previous weeks skipped. Re-target every threshold and easy prescription here to the zones the 08-11 time trial returned, not the numbers written below, if the test moved them.
weeks.methodology: Load is progressed in a wave rather than a straight line, because continuous accumulation eventually outruns the rate at which adaptation is realised - and that matters more than usual now that the volume band has been raised by 17%. When volume comes down, intensity is held or nudged up rather than cut alongside it: reduce the work, keep the signal. Threshold progresses by interval duration rather than pace, which is the correct variable when pace is anchored to a measurement. Gym-in-the-morning and run-in-the-afternoon keeps the two stimuli separated on double days, and plyometrics stay off hard-run days.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 50 min genuinely easy, at or below your current easy cap (138 bpm, or the re-anchored figure from the 08-11 TT).
sessions.purpose: Aerobic base volume opening the absorb week.
sessions.why: Easy volume is the part of the week that stays constant while harder work fluctuates, so it anchors the absorb week rather than absorbing the cut itself. Not extended, since the point of this week is that total load steps back.

sessions.title: Threshold 4x8' + Heavy Lower (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no gym) THRESHOLD: 15 min easy warmup -> 4x8 min @ threshold with 2:30 jog recovery -> 10 min easy cooldown. Use the TT-anchored threshold pace/HR; the 155-163 bpm / 4:48-4:34/km figures below are the pre-test values. PM (gym): back squat 4x3 @ 100 kg (RPE 8, progress if >2 RIR); trap-bar deadlift 3x3 @ 130 kg; hip thrust 3x8 @ 110 kg. No plyometrics today.

steps.target: Z1, at or below easy cap
hold pace to the last rep

sessions.purpose: Progress threshold volume to 32 minutes at freshly measured intensity, while weekly load steps down.
sessions.why: Intensity is held through the absorb week on purpose: cutting volume and intensity together produces detraining rather than absorption, which is the same principle behind keeping intensity in a race-week freshen. 32 minutes is one rung above the previous week, a step small enough to be accumulation rather than a new stimulus. Full strength dose returns here because, unlike the TT week, the running session is submaximal and can carry it.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 50 min genuinely easy, at or below your easy cap. Home treadmill is fine - keep it flat and dull.
sessions.purpose: Recovery running between the week's two quality days.
sessions.why: The rule that hard days sit at least one easy day apart is what makes both of them worth doing. No strides or surges, because quality added here would turn a two-quality-day week into three grey days and blunt Thursday.

sessions.title: Base Compromised Sim (3 rounds)
sessions.prescription: AM (gym): 10 min easy warmup with drills (~1.7 km) -> 3 rounds of 800 m compromised run @ ~5:05/km into one station: R1 sled pull 153 kg / 50 m; R2 sandbag lunges 30 kg / 100 m; R3 wall balls 9 kg x 50 to 3.0 m. 5 min jog cooldown (~0.8 km).
sessions.purpose: Maintain station transitions and posterior-chain strength-endurance at a reduced dose.
sessions.why: Shortened to three rounds rather than dropped, because transition skill is cheap to maintain and expensive to rebuild. Rotated onto pulling and lunging so the reduced volume still refreshes movements the other weeks neglect. Effort stays moderate for the same reason as every base sim: the week already has its hard day.

sessions.title: Easy + Plyo Primer (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (gym, ~15 min): box jumps 3x3 + hurdle hops 3x5, full recovery. PM (home treadmill or outdoors): 45 min easy, at or below your easy cap.

steps.target: at or below easy cap, conversational

sessions.purpose: Maintenance plyometric dose plus easy aerobic km.
sessions.why: Contact volume drops with the rest of the week but the session stays, since elastic qualities are maintained by frequency more than by volume. Jumps in the morning on fresh legs, run in the afternoon - never the reverse, and never on Tuesday.

sessions.title: Long Run
sessions.prescription: 98 min continuous, aerobic throughout. First 30 min at easy cap, then 138-145 bpm (~5:30-5:50/km) for 55 min, last 13 min easy.
sessions.purpose: Extend long-run duration even while weekly volume steps back.
sessions.why: The long run grows by six minutes while the week shrinks, because long-run duration is the specific adaptation the 21k and Hyrox running both need and it is worth protecting from the absorb week's cut. The reduction is taken from the midweek easy days instead, where the km are more interchangeable.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Optional light mobility or an easy walk.
sessions.purpose: Consolidate three weeks at the raised volume band.
sessions.why: This is the rest day that closes the accumulation phase the final week builds on, so it matters most of the four. No active recovery prescribed.

weeks.rationale: Block peak, 11 weeks to Hyrox #2. Volume reaches 67 km - the top of the raised band and the highest week of the macrocycle so far - with threshold at its longest rung (4x9', 36 min), the sim back to five rounds in race order, and the race-pace finish restored to the long run. This is the week the block has been building toward and it should be the hardest of the four. If it lands cleanly, the ramp is working; if it does not, that is the signal to hold 62 rather than push higher in September.
weeks.methodology: After an absorb week the following week can carry the block's highest load, which is the entire reason for undulating rather than accumulating linearly. Threshold continues to progress by interval duration, the correct variable once pace is anchored to a measurement. The long run's race-pace finish returns now that base volume has been held for a month, adding specific endurance on pre-fatigued legs at a deliberately small dose. Heavy compound work stays paired to the hard run, plyometrics and upper-body strength stay on easy days, and stations stay at competition load - the qualities are separated by function so that none of them blunts another.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 56 min genuinely easy, at or below your easy cap. Split into 2x28 min AM/PM on the treadmill if a single run feels heavy this week.
sessions.purpose: Aerobic volume opening the block's biggest week.
sessions.why: The extra kilometres of the peak week go here, on the easy day, rather than into the quality sessions where they would raise intensity as well as load. The AM/PM split option exists precisely because the treadmill makes it free: same volume, lower per-session tissue stress, which is what makes the top of a raised band survivable.

sessions.title: Threshold 4x9' + Heavy Lower (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no gym) THRESHOLD: 15 min easy warmup -> 4x9 min @ threshold with 2:30 jog recovery -> 10 min easy cooldown. Use the TT-anchored threshold pace/HR. PM (gym): back squat 4x3 @ 100 kg (RPE 8, progress if >2 RIR); trap-bar deadlift 3x3 @ 130 kg; hip thrust 3x8 @ 110 kg. No plyometrics today.

steps.target: Z1, at or below easy cap
hold pace to the last rep - this is the block's hardest set

sessions.purpose: The block's largest threshold dose at 36 minutes, plus maintenance heavy lower.
sessions.why: 36 minutes is a 12% step from the previous week and the top of this block's ladder; going further belongs in September, after this volume has been held for a month. Duration is progressed rather than pace because the pace now comes from a measurement, and running faster than it would mean leaving threshold rather than training it. Strength volume stays flat all block since the goal is maintaining an already Pro-level quality, not adding hypertrophy that would compete with the running ramp for recovery.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 56 min genuinely easy, at or below your easy cap. Split AM/PM if preferred - this is a recovery run despite the distance, so keep it dull.
sessions.purpose: Aerobic volume separating the block's hardest threshold session from its biggest sim.
sessions.why: Carries a full 10 km on an easy day because that is how a 67 km week is built without adding a third quality session. The distance is only safe if the intensity is genuinely low, so the split option matters more here than anywhere else in the week.

sessions.title: Base Compromised Sim (5 rounds)
sessions.prescription: AM (gym): 10 min easy warmup with drills (~1.7 km) -> 5 rounds of 1000 m compromised run @ ~5:00/km into one station, in race order: R1 ski erg 1000 m; R2 sled push 202 kg / 50 m; R3 sled pull 153 kg / 50 m; R4 farmers carry 2x32 kg / 200 m; R5 wall balls 9 kg x 50 to 3.0 m. 5 min jog cooldown (~0.8 km).

steps.target: ~5:00/km, hold form when it gets ugly

sessions.purpose: Five full rounds of race-order station work with compromised running at competition loads.
sessions.why: Extended to five rounds because station volume is the safest place to add load in a peak week - it has no eccentric running cost and therefore does not compound the volume ramp. Pace nudges from 5:05 to 5:00/km, small enough that the session stays moderate rather than becoming a second hard day the week cannot absorb alongside 36 minutes of threshold. Run in race order so the transitions rehearsed are the ones that actually occur on the day.

sessions.title: Easy + Plyo + Heavy Upper (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (gym): box jumps 4x3 + hurdle hops 3x5, full recovery; then weighted pull-up 4x4 and overhead press 4x4 at RPE 8 (~2 RIR). No concrete loads are on file for upper work - pick the weight that lands at RPE 8 and LOG WHAT YOU USED so ATHLETE_LOADS can finally be filled in. PM (home treadmill or outdoors): 50 min easy, at or below your easy cap.

steps.target: RPE 8, ~2 RIR - LOG THE LOAD USED
RPE 8, ~2 RIR - LOG THE LOAD USED
at or below easy cap, conversational

sessions.purpose: Easy km, plyometric maintenance, and the block's upper-body strength touch for ski erg and sled pull.
sessions.why: Upper-body strength drives the ski erg and sled pull directly and is the least-trained quality on file, so it earns a place even in the biggest week - but on an easy day, in the morning, where it costs nothing. Still prescribed by RPE rather than kilograms because no upper loads have been recorded since the 2026-07-23 baseline was due; logging what gets used here is what makes the next block's prescription concrete. Placed Friday rather than Thursday so it does not compound station fatigue.

sessions.title: Long Run + Race-Pace Finish
sessions.prescription: 76 min easy (HR <=142 bpm, ~5:30-5:50/km) -> 4x3 min @ race pace (~4:55/km, or the TT-adjusted equivalent) with 2 min easy jog between -> 4 min easy cooldown.
sessions.purpose: Long aerobic run finished with race-pace running on pre-fatigued legs.
sessions.why: The race-pace finish returns after four weeks away, because the base volume it was traded for has now been banked and the block should close with its most specific session. Only twelve minutes of it, and only after 76 easy, so this stays an endurance run with a finish rather than a workout demanding its own recovery day. Race pace sits slower than threshold on purpose: this trains the pace actually held on race day after eight station stops, not the pace holdable for nine minutes fresh.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Review the block before the next one is generated: did 67 km land, and what did the TT change?
sessions.purpose: Close the block with full recovery and a review point.
sessions.why: The last day of a four-week block is the natural place to be genuinely empty, since the next block should start from absorbed work rather than accumulated fatigue. It is also the review gate: whether this week felt sustainable decides if base_weekly_km climbs again in September or holds at 62.
